speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan
text: asked the Minister for Health (a) what portion of an average bill for a surgical procedure in each Table for Surgical Procedures, including pre-operation scans, medical tests and other work-ups as well as post-operation rehabilitation, is paid through MediSave; (b) what portion of this average bill is paid out-of-pocket; and (c) whether MediShield Life coverage for surgical procedures can be further enhanced for a member above 80 years old, beyond the present recommended deductibles for day surgeries.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Koh Poh Koon) (for the Minister for Health)
text: MediShield Life is targeted at helping patients with more costly bills.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Koh Poh Koon) (for the Minister for Health)
text: The bulk of it is still taken care by subsidies and the remaining by the other components I just illustrated.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Koh Poh Koon) (for the Minister for Health)
text: So, eight in 10 Singaporean subsidised bills cost less than $100 in cash.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Koh Poh Koon) (for the Minister for Health)
text: The MediShield Life and MediSave claim limits for surgical procedures are pegged to the complexity of the surgery required, as indicated in the Table of Surgical Procedures.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Koh Poh Koon) (for the Minister for Health)
text: The MediShield Life Council has recommended further adjustments to the claim limits for daily ward and treatment charges as part of the ongoing MediShield Life Review.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Koh Poh Koon) (for the Minister for Health)
text: And we will also review MediSave limits in tandem with this.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Koh Poh Koon) (for the Minister for Health)
text: These adjustments will help to cover more of the inpatient or day surgery bill.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Koh Poh Koon) (for the Minister for Health)
text: This will help older patients with exceptionally large bills due to long or multiple periods of hospitalisation within that same year.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Koh Poh Koon) (for the Minister for Health)
text: We will continue to review the MediShield Life and the MediSave limits regularly, to ensure they remain adequate in protecting Singaporeans, while keeping the premiums affordable.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Koh Poh Koon) (for the Minister for Health)
text: MediFund, as I said earlier in a previous reply, is available for needy Singaporeans who require additional financial assistance to pay for their healthcare bills after subsidies, after MediSave and after MediShield Life.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Koh Poh Koon) (for the Minister for Health)
text: So, I want to emphasise that point again – no Singaporean will be denied appropriate healthcare.

speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong)
text: I recently saw an estimated bill for a procedure in the highest surgical table, table 7, and assuming a C class ward stay, the out-of-pocket expense, meaning the cash outlay after MediSave and MediShield Life claim was estimated to be $9,000.

speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong)
text: My question is: were outlier surgical bills in the scope of the Council's review?

speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong)
text: And, if so, what were the conclusions of this review regarding the adequacy of MediShield Life coverage for such outlier bills?

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: Because the policyholder has a deductible a year and the deductible, usually, is in range of $3,000.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: So, for the policyholder to have to pay $9,000 in cash, I think it is quite unusual.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: So, we do need to take out a look at the specifics of the case whether they have required very esoteric or specialised treatment even though they may be a C Class patient where certain treatments would not fall within the scope of the usual subsidies, for example.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: I think that is something we can do.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: And if the person does have difficulties paying the bill with cash, then this is where we need to get a medical social worker involved and see if MediFund can be a way to help defray the cost and help this person to settle the hospital bills and continue the treatment.
